issue: Must an appellate court raise the waiver created by an unconditional guilty plea (which bars review of nonjurisdictional pretrial rulings such as a denied suppression motion) on its own when the government does not invoke it, or is the plea a jurisdictional bar enforced sua sponte?

sides.position: An unconditional guilty plea is jurisdictional, so the appellate court must enforce the bar sua sponte even if the government does not raise it.
cases: United States v. Combs, 657 F.3d 565 (7th Cir. 2011)

sides.position: An unconditional guilty plea is a nonjurisdictional, waivable claim-processing rule. The government can forfeit it by not raising it, and the court is not required to enforce it sua sponte.
cases: United States v. Jacobo Castillo, 496 F.3d 947 (9th Cir. 2007) (en banc)
United States v. De Vaughn, 694 F.3d 1141 (10th Cir. 2012)
United States v. Spaeth, 69 F.4th 1190 (10th Cir. 2023)

quote: On that point, our sister circuits split.
cite: United States v. Riojas, 139 F.4th 465 (5th Cir. 2025)
